newsitem.title: USA: DNC chairman asked Huang for favor - report.
newsitem.headline: DNC chairman asked Huang for favor - report.

text.p: Suspended Democratic National Committee fund-raiser John Huang arranged special treatment for the daughter of the Democratic National Committee chairman when she visited Indonesia, the Washington Post reported in Sunday editions.

Donald Fowler, DNC general chairman, asked fund-raiser John Huang to have his daughter met at the airport on a visit to Indonesia in May. Huang, suspended last month after reports he unlawfully solicited contributions, was a former Commerce Department official and former employee of the Lippo Group of Indonesia.
Cynthia Fowler, a 26-year-old graduate student, was met by an executive of the Lippo Group, the financial conglomerate tied to more than $500,000 in recent contributions to the DNC.
She told the Post a Lippo helicopter flew her to her hotel, where she stayed for two days at Lippo expense.
The company also paid for tickets on a domestic airline that flew her on two side trips, while the executive served as her interpreter, the Post reported.
The Post quoted Fowler as saying there was nothing improper about Lippo's hospitality. He said he did not instruct Huang to arrange first-class treatment, and only learned about it after the fact.

"I did not ask for anything other than for somebody to meet her at the airport and to make sure she got to her hotel," the paper quoted Fowler as saying. "Trying to involve my daughter in this (is) just preposterous," he said.
Huang's fund-raising activities have come under scrutiny after the DNC returned a $250,000 contribution after reports that it came from a South Korean business, not its U.S. subsidiary.
